title: Minimum Flips to Make a OR b Equal to c
summary: Given three positive numbers a, b, and c, determine the minimum number of bit flips required in the binary representations of a and b to make the bitwise OR of a and b equal to c.
statement: Given three positive numbers a, b, and c, determine the minimum number of bit flips required in the binary representations of a and b to make the bitwise OR of a and b equal to c. A bit flip operation changes a single bit from 1 to 0 or from 0 to 1.
constraints: Flip individual bits in a or b until a OR b equals c.
Return the minimum number of flips.
hints: Bits are independent, so minimize each position separately.
For target zero, flip every one among a and b; for target one, flip once only when both are zero.
Shift all three integers until no bits remain.
Summing independent per-bit minima gives the global minimum.
editorial: Summing independent per-bit minima gives the global minimum.

tests.explanation: Only the low bit must be set, so one flip is enough.
